name: Quantum state classification benchmark
description: Quantum computing is a growing field where the information is processed by two-levels quantum states known as qubits. Current physical realizations of qubits require a careful calibration, composed by different experiments, due to noise and decoherence phenomena. Among the different characterization experiments, a crucial step is to develop a model to classify the measured state by discriminating the ground state from the excited state. In this proceedings we benchmark multiple classification techniques applied to real quantum devices.
evaluation_method: Accuracy (primary), with complementary metrics such as precision, recall, and ROC-AUC for imbalanced cases
general_score_metric: Classification accuracy (percentage of correctly identified ground vs. excited states)
reputation: Niche benchmark targeted at the quantum-hardware/signal-processing community; useful for readout-model comparisons but not yet broadly adopted outside that community.
notes: Device- and experiment-specific data lead to limited cross-device generalization; small and hardware-dependent datasets; not an LLM benchmark; performance can vary widely with calibration and noise.
